name: New Orleans by Night Notable Locations (Lore)

text.content: Jackson Square, bordered by Chartres, St. Ann, Decatur and St. Peter Streets, is New Orleans' best-known Elysium and the traditional heart of the French Quarter, including the St. Louis Cathedral, the Presbytere and the Cabildo. Kindred of the city customarily meet in the Square itself or in the Cabildo's back rooms, a tradition Prince Doran maintained for decades until a suspicious 1988 fire gutted its top floor and roof — on the same night Justicar Xaviar had reportedly scheduled a meeting there. Gangrel Justicar Xaviar has also used the Square to host portions of his triennial Conclave.

pages.name: St. Louis Cemetery I (Marie Laveau's Tomb)

text.content: The oldest of New Orleans' aboveground necropoli, St. Louis Cemetery I on Basin and St. Louis Streets holds tombs dating to the mid-1700s and includes the monolithic, X-marked tomb of the historical Voodoo Queen Marie Laveau, who spent over 40 years resisting Setite infiltration of the city's Voodoo cults before age finally undid her. Like many of the city's older cemeteries, its neglected vaults and open tombs make convenient temporary havens for refugee Kindred, so long as they abide by the prince's rules.

pages.name: Storyville and the Ghost of Mariline

text.content: Once the notorious Red Light District bridging Basin, Conti and Iberville Streets, Storyville was destroyed by Prince Doran's order in 1917 after a renegade vampire fleeing a Blood Hunt elsewhere committed a string of gruesome, bloodless killings there, embarrassing the refugee Kindred who failed to report him. One victim, the prostitute Mariline, murdered in 1916, still haunts the old district as a spectral lure: Kindred who see her ghost feel drawn to follow the overpowering scent of blood as her throat re-opens in a spectral wound, a phenomenon that has only grown stronger with the decades. Doran decreed the area off-limits to feeding, a rule most Kindred still observe if only to avoid the risk of a witch-hunter learning to use Mariline as bait.

A once-fashionable resort on the southern shore of Lake Pontchartrain, the Lakeside Hotel fell into disrepair before an unknown benefactor secretly bought it for the Followers of Set, whose leader Blood Bound the new owner as a Retainer. The rundown hotel now serves as the front for Manon's Setite temple; the Setites and their Retainers deliberately abuse or frighten off any mortal guests who wander in, preserving the appearance of a failing but legitimate business while smuggling operations continue on the docks below.

An abandoned riverboat refurbished by Prince Marcel into an invitation-only floating nightclub, the Delta Night operates only a few weeks a year — during Carnival, the prince's mortal birthday, and other occasions of importance — moored in a secluded bayou past Destrehan Plantation. Guests are treated to the finest music, gambling and performance New Orleans' Kindred underworld can offer, all staffed by Marcel's most trusted servants.

pages.name: City Park and Bayou St. John

text.content: City Park, at the end of Esplanade Avenue, was once New Orleans' most popular dueling ground and now hosts a quiet three-way contest between Kindred, mages and the Uktena werewolves for a caern buried within its grounds. The adjoining Bayou St. John, the last true bayou remaining within city limits, was ceded to the Lupines by the original 18th-century land treaty but has since been swallowed by the city's growth; Kindred use it to dispose of Lupine dead without realizing the Uktena consider the bayou sacred burial ground in its own right.

A Toreador-run strip club on Bourbon Street, the Lamp Light caters to mortals until the small hours, after which selected nights close to kine entirely for performances ending in a public Kiss. The mortal performers — disparagingly called “vampire whores” by the Kindred who watch them — willingly submit for the euphoria of the bite, chosen carefully by the club's manager so that no one loses consciousness onstage.

Several miles west of the city, the Guilbeau family's antebellum plantation, Rubis d'le Nuit, serves as Prince Marcel's primary haven and, unofficially, as the retreat of his silent elder brother and sire's-childe Jereaux, who most Kindred believe never truly left the family estate after Doran's death. Marcel is known to retire to the plantation for days at a time whenever a difficult decision needs to be made — and whenever a serious threat to his rule needs to quietly disappear.

pages.name: Our Lady of the Holy Cross (Inquisition Cell)

text.content: A small Catholic coed school southwest of the city, at the edge of Uktena territory, secretly hosts one of the Society of Leopold's more unusual cells. Sister Louise DeChambeau of the Order of St. Joan came to Holy Cross investigating what she calls the “Werewolf Threat,” and while the Lupines have consumed most of her attention, she is increasingly convinced vampires also lurk in New Orleans and means to turn the Inquisition's eye on them next.

vtmlarp.source: New Orleans by Night, Chapters One & Three
